_comment: Milestone E — trusted, out-of-agent credential→scope source (AC-40 / AC-40a / AC-55).
Maps a credential ALIAS (ARN, key-id, secret name) to a stable secret-store id, then
the COLLISION-RESISTANT canonical identity (sha256 of the stable id) to the scope.
Two aliases of ONE physical credential canonicalize to one identity → one scope (AC-55).
The agent process cannot assert a narrower scope for a broader credential; GATE 3 reads
the scope from THIS source keyed by the canonical identity, never from an agent hint.
The `<canonical-identity-of ...>` placeholders are sha256(stableId); the e2e fixture
_scopedCredentials_comment: DEPLOYMENT-CONFIG scoped-credential DECLARATION (AC-40 / AC-50) — which spawn
delivery-channel credentials are scoped, and to which trusted alias. Because this
is hashed into the signed manifest (AC-36), it is NOT agent-writable: a compromised
agent cannot declare its own scoping nor un-scope a credential to smuggle it past
GATE 3. When the anchor is pinned and this block is present, GATE 3 AUTO-ACTIVATES on
a real spawn from config alone (no RunOptions.policyGate3 needed) — the scoped env var
is delivered ONLY with a valid CommandAuthorization, else its channel is omitted.
